text:
sophia_sales: Heads-up — during the Acme enterprise POC demo we started getting intermittent 503/504s around 2026-03-20T21:02Z. Demo had to pause. Attaching quick details below.

jamal_support: On it. Can you paste the curl you used and approx rps/burst shape? Also which model/route was called?

sophia_sales: Repro curl: ```curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-xl-2","input":"Summarize...","stream":false}'```  Burst was customer load test -> ~120RPS peak for ~30s, then drop.

alex_infra: I pulled the node logs for that window. We're seeing queue growth + autoscale delay. Snippet: 
```[2026-03-20T21:02:14Z] ERROR request=abcd123 status=503 reason="backend-overloaded" queue_length=1257 cpu=92%
[2026-03-20T21:02:16Z] WARN autoscaler cooldown active threshold=80% window=60s current_util=85%
[2026-03-20T21:02:18Z] ERROR request=ef01 status=504 upstream_timeout
```
Queue lingered >1000 for ~45s which caused timeouts.

jamal_support: Is burstpool enabled for this tenant? Any failover policy configured?

alex_infra: Burstpool for this account is 0 right now (not linked to reserved capacity). Failover policy = "none" (sales requested no auto-model-switch during demo). Autoscaler is conservative to avoid noisy spin-ups.

jamal_support: Ok — that explains it. Two short mitigation options: 1) enable temporary burstpool / immediate scale-up, 2) enable soft-fallback to quantized variant (rwd-xl-2-quant) to shed latency/cost. Which is acceptable?

elaine_security: Quick sec note — quantized variant still runs in us-west-2 and uses same encryption at rest/in transit. It's fine for POC from a data-residency perspective, we just need to note it in the security questionnaire for compliance.

sophia_sales: Customer is nervous about surprise billing if we switch models or scale. Any guidance?

jamal_support: Short-term: explain this is a temporary mitigation. We can keep them on a capped burst pool + notify about potential token delta. For long-term, link reserved burstpool to enterprise deals to avoid this.

deploy-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1842012345 "acme-poc-throttle" (priority: P2)

alex_infra: I'm applying changes now: - set autoscale threshold 80%->60% (temp) - add +4 GPU burstpool for this tenant - enable soft-fallback to rwd-xl-2-quant for requests >2s latency. Pushing in 30s, rolling config out. Will monitor metrics.

jamal_support: Please also add a short 5min retention trace header so we can link traces in logs. @sophia_sales ask Acme to send the failing trace id if they hit it again (X-Trace header).

sophia_sales: Will request trace header from them, should have reply in ~10m. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: ALERT: 503 error rate dropped below 1% for 5m — incident INC-2026-1842012345 resolved at 1842012478

jamal_support: Root-cause summary for notes: sudden traffic burst + conservative autoscale cooldown + no burstpool + failover disabled => queue buildup => 5xx.

Action items (owners):
- Link reserved burstpool for enterprise POCs (alex_infra)
- Product: add a soft-fallback toggle for demos + doc update (jamal_support/product)
- Sales: update pricing FAQ for model-switch during failover and call it out in security/contract docs (sophia_sales)
- Security: annotate quantized-model use in questionnaire (elaine_security)

We'll follow up with a short write-up for Acme and the internal deal page.

sophia_sales: Thanks team — I’ll coordinate comms and confirm with the customer.
